en: Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to me: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us: Hammad—meaning Ibn Zayd—narrated to us: Ma'bad ibn Hilal al-'Anazi narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, that a man asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), saying: 'When will the Hour be established?' He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) remained silent for a little while, then looked at a boy in front of him from Azd Shanu'ah and said: 'If this boy lives a long life, old age will not overtake him before the Hour is established.' He said: Anas said: That boy was of my peers on that day.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, that a man asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): 'When will the Hour be established?' while there was a boy from the Ansar with him called Muhammad. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'If this boy lives, perhaps old age will not overtake him before the Hour is established.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: When the bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), they would ask him about the Hour: 'When is the Hour?' So he looked at the youngest person among them and said: 'If this one lives, old age will not overtake him before your hour comes upon you.'

Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i narrated to us: Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from Ma'bad, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'I and the Hour have been sent like these two.' He said: And he joined his index finger and middle finger.

And Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Hamzah—meaning ad-Dabbi—and Abu at-Tayyah, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of their hadith.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us [H]; and Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu at-Tayyah, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with this.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Khalid—meaning Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Qatadah and Abu at-Tayyah narrating that they both heard Anas narrating that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'I and the Hour have been sent like this.' And Shu'bah joined his index and middle fingers, demonstrating it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Qatadah; Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'I and the Hour have been sent like these two.' Shu'bah said: And I heard Qatadah saying in his storytelling: 'like the superiority of one of them over the other,' and I do not know whether he mentioned it from Anas or Qatadah said it of his own accord.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman and 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... [H]; and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us—and the wording is his: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, that he heard Sahl saying: I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) gesturing with the finger next to the thumb and the middle finger while saying: 'I and the Hour have been sent like this.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: 'Abd ar-Rahman—meaning Ibn Mahdi—narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'The Hour will not be established except upon the worst of people.'
And Abu Kamil narrated it to me: Hammad narrated to us, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, from Mu'alla ibn Ziyad, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) [H]; and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated it to us: Hammad narrated to us, from al-Mu'alla ibn Ziyad, tracing it back to Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, tracing it back to Ma'qil ibn Yasar, tracing it back to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'Worship during turmoil is like emigration to me.'

And Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us, both saying: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Umayyah ibn Bistam al-'Ayshi narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Ziyad ibn Riyah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'Hasten to perform deeds before six things: the Dajjal, the smoke, the beast of the earth, the rising of the sun from its west, the public affair, and the private concern of one of you.'

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, saying: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Hasten to perform deeds before six things: the rising of the sun from its west, or the smoke, or the Dajjal, or the beast, or the private concern of one of you, or the public affair.'

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far ar-Raqqi narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from a group of three from his people among whom was Abu Qatadah, who said: We used to pass by Hisham ibn 'Amir on our way to 'Imran ibn Husayn... the like of the hadith of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Mukhtar, except that he said: 'a matter greater than the Dajjal.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Hadrami narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn al-Mukhtar—narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from a group of people among whom were Abu ad-Dahma' and Abu Qatadah, who said: We used to pass by Hisham ibn 'Amir on our way to 'Imran ibn Husayn. So he said one day: 'You bypass me to go to men who were no more present with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) than I was, nor more knowledgeable of his hadith than I am. I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Between the creation of Adam and the onset of the Hour, there is no creation greater than the Dajjal."'
And Muhammad ibn Bashshar and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated it to us, both saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, with this chain of narration.

Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu az-Zubayr narrated to me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: Umm Sharik informed me that she heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'The people will surely flee from the Dajjal into the mountains.' Umm Sharik said: 'O Messenger of Allah, where will the Arabs be on that day?' He said: 'They will be few.'

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us: Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah, from his paternal uncle Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Seventy thousand of the Jews of Isfahan wearing Persian shawls will follow the Dajjal.'

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said... and he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: 'So he comes to the salty barren ground of al-Jurf and pitches his tent,' and he said: 'and every hypocrite man and hypocrite woman will come out to him.'

'Ali ibn Hujr as-Sa'di narrated to me: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Abu 'Amr—meaning al-Awza'i—narrated to me, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'There is no town that the Dajjal will not enter except Mecca and Medina; there is no mountain pass of their mountain passes except that there are angels lined up in ranks guarding it. Then he will alight at the salty barren ground, and Medina will shake with three tremors, whereupon every disbeliever and hypocrite will come out to him from it.'

Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Al-Mughirah—meaning al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu az-Zinad, from ash-Sha'bi, from Fatimah bint Qays, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sat on the pulpit and said: 'O people, Tamim ad-Dari narrated to me that some people from his folk were at sea in a ship of theirs and it was wrecked with them, so some of them rode upon a plank among the planks of the ship and emerged onto an island in the sea...' and he conveyed the hadith.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and Ahmad ibn 'Uthman an-Nawfali narrated to us, both saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us: my father narrated to us, saying: I heard Ghaylan ibn Jarir narrating from ash-Sha'bi, from Fatimah bint Qays, who said: Tamim ad-Dari came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and informed the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) that he traveled by sea and his ship was lost with him, so he landed on an island. He went out onto it seeking water and met a person dragging his hair... and he recounted the hadith and said in it: 'Then he said: "As for me, if permission to come out were given to me, I would tread all the lands except Taybah." So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) brought him out to the people and he narrated to them; he said: "This is Taybah, and that is the Dajjal."'

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith al-Hujaymi Abu 'Uthman narrated to us: Qurrah narrated to us: Sayyar Abu al-Hakam narrated to us: Ash-Sha'bi narrated to us, saying: We visited Fatimah bint Qays, and she offered us fresh dates called Rutab Ibn Tab, and gave us barley meal drink to drink. I asked her about a woman divorced three times: where should she observe her waiting period? She said: 'My husband divorced me three times, so the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) permitted me to observe the waiting period in my family's house.' She said: 'Then an announcement was made to the people: "The prayer is in congregation!"' She said: 'So I went along with those of the people who went.' She said: 'I was in the front row of the women, which was directly behind the rear row of the men.' She said: 'And I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) delivering a sermon while on the pulpit, saying: "Indeed, cousins of Tamim ad-Dari traveled by sea..."' and he conveyed the hadith, and added in it: She said: 'It is as if I am looking at the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) as he struck the ground with his staff and said: "This is Taybah," meaning Medina.'
